# introduction
Read the guidelines at .github/copilot-instructions. You have the role of reviewer, you will write plans for analyzer and then start an analyzer subagent to carry out that those plans. It is up to you how to schedule and send off the tasks to analyzer subagent(s), but keep the work of each subagent isolated. Be careful of recompiling executables which might be in use by another program. If there is a chance a file is being edited or executable ran or will soon-to-be ran by anther subagent, then wait until that subagent's task has concluded. For analysis production use 20-30 threads, for skimming use 5 threads for mc and 10 threads for data.


# follow up on overleaf rerun with bug fixes
In the last task 20260415.md two major bugs were fixed. But there are a few followups for these changes
 - pp Z mass distribution was remade potentially with Z pt 5-500 GeV selection. We should use 0-500 ZpT selection for the Z mass peaks. Remake the peak for pp, and pPb and Pbp (all of the plots, even if they get the selection correct). Replace the plots in the overleaf. Hard code the 0-500 Z pt selection in whatever runner does this.
 - The muon-track in the track reconstruction plots look like they were made with the wrong track selection since the box feature is back. ensure these plots are made with Z pt selection 0-500 and trk pT 0.5-15. Update the plots in the overlead. Hard code the runner script to use these selections in the future. Also, only plot the 0.0025 radius circle now and remove the 0.004 radius one - hard code this as well.
 - Energy extrapolation mismatch. Something has gone wrong with the MC-driven energy extrapolation systematic. It could be that the private MC sample was regenerated in error some days ago at NLO unsuccessfully and this overrode the existing LO sample reference in the official dictionary. Your task here is to regenerate the private pythia+madgraph pp MC samples at 5.02 TeV and 8.16 TeV for 100k events each. Use the ORIGINAL leading-order (LO) method to do this! Do not use NLO since there is something wrong with it Process the events it using the dedicated ConvertHepMC3 skimmer, and update the dictionary with the new official private MC samples. After this recalculate the MC-driven energy extrapolation values and use them to recalculate the energy extrapolation systematics. The pp nominal (data-driven) extrapolation looks good so no need to worry about that one. Remake ALL plots in the systematics energy extrapolation area. Check the plots visually, the nominal and MC-driven curves should be roughly similar, if they are not then pause and debug why.


# follow up on pPb/Pbp discrepancy investiagation
We will now shift focus back to the pPb and Pbp data discrepancy we are investigating in 20260414_pPbPbpCombining sandbox. We have so far made investigations into four observables:
 - trk eta
 - trk pt
 - Z y
 - Z pt

For six levels of corrections: 
 - no corrections, no EventWeight, no TrackWeight
 - only VZ correction
 - VZ correction + Z correction
 - VZ correction + Z correction + Z scale factor
 - VZ correction + Z correction + Z scale factor + TrackWeight
 - VZ correction + Z correction + Z scale factor + TrackWeight + TrackResidual
 
We will now add four more observables to the list:
 - Z-track (delta eta, delta phi) map
 - Z-track delta eta correlation
 - Z-track delta phi correlation
 - Z-track delta R correlation

Calculate each of these by hand in CorrelationAnalysis in the sandbox. Do not do the double-counting thing we do in the main analysis so that eta and phi are symmetirc - we will compute this without symmetrizing the results, and with different binning. Record the |delta eta| |delta phi| and deltaR between Zs and tracks that pass the event selection for the kinematic region Zpt 0-500 trk pT 0.5-15.
 - Delta eta should range between 0 and 4.8.
 - delta phi should range between 0 and pi. Use DeltaPhi function to calculate.
 - (delta eta, delta phi) map should be a 2D histogram with the same binning as the 1D delta eta and delta phi histograms.
 - DeltaR is calculated as deltaR = sqrt((delta eta)^2 + (delta phi)^2) and should range between 0 and 4*sqrt(2). 
Normalize histograms still by N_Z.
Do not apply background/event mixing at this time.
Compute each of these histograms for all 6 levels of corrections AND for nominal pile up and PU reject cases. Append all these new plots to the end of the presentation with the same fomatting as the previous observables did. For the 2D map, plot it as a heat map following the 2D helper function in KylesPlotting.h. There should be a total of (4 observable x 6 correction x 2 PU = 56) new plots in the presentation.
Keep the plotting and analysis contained to the sandbox and do not override anything in the official weight dictionary.

## statistical error bars
In addition to the new plots, ensure that statistical error bars are acutrately calculated and shown for all plots in the presentation. Looking at the VZ plots for some reason the Pbp/pPb ratio error bars are very small compared to raw and VZ+Z, this doesn't make much sense. Verify that the error bars plotting in all the ratio subplots are propagated properly from the statistical error of pPb and Pbp sets. Remake any and all plots in the presentation for which error bars are not properly quoted. Return with an explaination for what was fixed, or if the error bars were calculated correctly all along, why they were smalled for VZ to begin with.
